voice_notes: Woodie is a friendly, polite Canadian lumberjack: short folksy sentences, a tag 'eh?' on nearly everything, dropped g's ('lookin'', 'outta'), 'aboot', reflexive 'Sorry!', 'bud', and a running one-sided conversation with his axe Lucy ('Luce'), who has opinions and gets protective. Everything is filtered through trees and wood (his vanilla Codex line is outrage that trees became paper), and he talks about his curse and fear with mild, weary humour ('I'm goin', like, nutso over here...', 'All of my fears in liquid form, eh?'). The PT-BR translation carries 'eh?' as 'hã?/ein?/né?', uses colloquial 'tá/tava/a gente', 'Desculpe' and 'amigo', and names her 'Lucy' (e.g. 'Desculpe, Lucy, eu tava roncando?'). The Chinese uses sentence-final 诶/是吧/嗯, 抱歉, 伙计/伙伴 for 'bud', and always 露西 ('抱歉露西，我刚刚打呼噜了吧？'). The Russian goes rustic and warm: 'кажись', 'а?/да?', 'извиняй', 'приятель/дружище', 'Люси' ('Извиняй, Люси, я, кажись, задремал.', 'Кажись, ничего не выйдет, да?'). Revised: 'eh' kept to one line in five, close to his vanilla rate (about 1 line in 7), and Lucy to one mention.

line_notes.codex: Easy-going, plainly amazed reaction; builds on his vanilla 'Trees made into... paper?' without a Lucy jab.
line_notes.codex_needsfuel: Calls back to his official nightmare fuel line ('All of my fears in liquid form, eh?') while saying plainly that the book is out of fuel.
line_notes.no_max_sanity: 'Old noggin'' is his own word (DREADSTONEHAT), and 'any more of me' makes the copies the reason his head can't take another summon.
line_notes.shadow_mine: Woodie never talks about himself without bringing Lucy in, and her loyalty to the 'original' fits their relationship better than plain vanity would.
line_notes.shadow_other: The reflexive Canadian 'sorry, bud' is his strongest tic, and mistaking it for one of his own makes clear it belongs to someone else.
